questions.question: Which package registry types does the official MCP Registry support? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: npm (registry.npmjs.org)
PyPI (pypi.org)
NuGet (api.nuget.org)
Docker/OCI images (Docker Hub, ghcr.io, *.pkg.dev, *.azurecr.io, mcr.microsoft.com)
Private Artifactory instances

questions.explanation: npm, PyPI, NuGet, OCI, and MCPB (GitHub/GitLab releases) are supported. Private package registries are explicitly out — private servers belong in a self-hosted registry.

questions.question: Match the ownership-verification markers to their package types — which pairings are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: npm: mcpName property in package.json matching the server.json name
PyPI: 'mcp-name: <server-name>' string in the package README (may be in an HTML comment)
NuGet: 'mcp-name: <server-name>' string in the package README
Docker/OCI: io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name annotation/LABEL on the image
MCPB: a GPG signature over the archive

questions.explanation: A–D are the documented markers. MCPB verification requires the identifier URL to contain 'mcp' plus a fileSha256 hash (validated by clients, not GPG).

questions.question: What does the MCP Registry provide? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A single place for server creators to publish metadata
Namespace management through DNS/GitHub verification
A REST API for clients and aggregators to discover servers
Standardized installation and configuration information
Hosting of the server code and binaries themselves

questions.explanation: The registry hosts metadata that points to packages; the code lives on npm, PyPI, Docker Hub, etc.

questions.question: Which spam-prevention and trust mechanisms does the official registry use today? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Namespace authentication (GitHub, DNS, or HTTP challenges) before publishing
Character limits and regex validation on free-form fields
Manual takedown of spam or malicious servers per the moderation policy
Delegating code security scanning to package registries and downstream aggregators
Mandatory human security audit of every published server

questions.explanation: A–D describe the current model. The registry explicitly does not audit server code itself — scanning is delegated to package registries and aggregators.

questions.question: Which mcp-publisher commands and behaviors are real? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: mcp-publisher init — scaffold a server.json with auto-detected values
mcp-publisher login github — authenticate for io.github.* namespaces
mcp-publisher publish --dry-run — validate without publishing
mcp-publisher logout — removes the local token file (without server-side revocation)
mcp-publisher verify — checks the server.json is valid before init

questions.explanation: All four commands behave as described — E is genuinely correct.

questions.question: Which namespace/authentication pairings are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: io.github.alice/* — GitHub OAuth login as alice (or her org)
com.acme/* — DNS or HTTP challenge proving control of acme.com
Remote URLs under com.acme/* must live on acme.com or its subdomains
io.github.* remotes have no URL restriction
io.github.* namespaces allow any remote URL regardless of verification

questions.explanation: GitHub namespaces bind to accounts, domain namespaces bind to DNS/HTTP proof, and the remote-URL restriction applies only to domain namespaces. All true.

questions.question: Which server types can be published to the OFFICIAL registry? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: An open-source npm package anyone can install
A closed-source but publicly downloadable Docker image
A publicly reachable remote server with no installable package
A server on a private package registry reachable only inside the corporate network
All of the above

questions.explanation: Open or closed source is fine as long as installation or access is public; private-network servers belong in a self-hosted registry.

questions.question: Which statements describe the intended consumption model of the registry? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Downstream aggregators pull metadata on a regular but infrequent basis (e.g., hourly)
Aggregators add curation, ratings, or extra metadata the official registry deliberately omits
Host applications should consume aggregators (via the shared OpenAPI spec), not the official registry directly
The official codebase is designed and supported for self-hosting private forks
All of the above

questions.explanation: The maintainers explicitly do NOT support self-hosting the official codebase — forkers are on their own; private registries should implement the OpenAPI spec instead.
